name: Founder Institute Bangladesh
benefits: Peer working groups and office hours
cohortTiming: Bangladesh Fall 2026: final application deadline 6 October; program runs from 27 October 2026 to Demo Day on 3 February 2027.
costOrEquity: Bangladesh entrance fee: Not publicly stated. Participating companies that join FI's Equity Collective issue a 2.5% warrant to the collective.
applicationPath: Apply through the Bangladesh Fall 2026 program page before 6 October 2026.
notes: A 15-week, in-person company-building programme for Bangladesh founders moving from an idea or early product towards traction and funding readiness. Weekly sprints cover customer validation, product development, launch, growth and fundraising, with recurring mentor reviews and investor feedback.

name: Orange Corners Bangladesh
benefits: Grants of up to €5,000 for selected participants
cohortTiming: Cohort 8 began on 29 July 2026; the next application window has not been announced.
costOrEquity: No application fee; grants and soft loans do not take equity.
applicationPath: Wait for the next Bangladesh intake announcement before applying. At least one founder must be Bangladeshi, aged 18–35 and based in Bangladesh.
notes: A Netherlands-backed programme helping young Bangladeshi founders build sustainable, investment-ready businesses that contribute to the Sustainable Development Goals. Its incubation track supports businesses that have already launched; graduates can progress to acceleration and financing support.

name: YY Ventures Incubation
cohortTiming: Programme-specific; applications for YY Goshthi are currently closed.
costOrEquity: Current fee and equity terms: Not publicly stated. The now-closed YY Goshthi programme advertised BDT 1–1.5 million in pre-seed investment for selected businesses.
applicationPath: Email info@yy.ventures about current incubation opportunities; the YY Goshthi application is closed.
notes: YY Ventures incubates early-stage, cause-driven businesses tackling social or environmental problems. Its model combines founder training, tailored consulting, workspace, business services and investor introductions to help teams launch an MVP and raise seed capital.

name: Impact Hub Dhaka
cohortTiming: No standing accelerator cohort; opportunities are announced programme by programme.
costOrEquity: Workspace pricing and programme terms vary.
applicationPath: No standing accelerator application is open; check the Projects page for partner-led programmes and apply through the relevant programme notice.
notes: A Dhaka-based workspace and innovation community connecting entrepreneurs and impact organisations with mentors, corporate partners, investors and public-sector institutions. It hosts partner-led incubation and acceleration programmes, but it is not itself a single recurring accelerator.

name: BYLC Ventures
cohortTiming: Cohort-based; no current application window is announced.
costOrEquity: No application fee. A BDT 200,000 programme and professional-services fee is deducted from the BDT 800,000 seed funding. Equity terms: Not publicly stated.
applicationPath: Apply through the BYLC Ventures page when the next cohort opens; shortlisted teams enter a selection bootcamp.
notes: A six-month accelerator and investment programme combining early-stage capital with founder leadership, company-building and Bangladesh-specific legal and financial support. It is sector-agnostic, prefers teams with some market traction and looks for businesses addressing socioeconomic challenges.

name: NSU Startups Next
benefits: Weekly KPI tracking and progress reviews every two weeks
NSU workspace plus programme tools and credits
Investor pitch and two months of post-programme support for Flagship teams
cohortTiming: Cohort 4 launched in May 2026 and was still active on 9 August 2026. Its 15 April application deadline has passed; the next intake has not been announced.
costOrEquity: No programme fee, according to the official FAQ. Equity terms: Not publicly stated.
applicationPath: Cohort 4 applications are closed. Follow the official website or LinkedIn page, or email nsu.sn@northsouth.edu, for the next intake. Eligibility varies by cohort.
notes: North South University's cohort-based startup platform has two 16-week tracks. Founders’ Lab helps idea-stage teams validate a business model and develop an initial MVP. Flagship Incubation supports launched, technology-enabled startups with early traction as they work towards product-market fit and investor readiness. Support includes structured reviews, mentors, workspace, tools and credits, investor exposure and two months of post-programme support for Flagship graduates.

name: Bangladesh Hi-Tech Park Authority (BHTPA)
cohortTiming: Facility- and programme-specific; BHTPA does not run one standing national accelerator cohort.
applicationPath: Use BHTPA's One Stop Service for park and incubation services and follow BHTPA notices for cohort-based programmes.
notes: The government authority that develops and manages hi-tech parks, software technology parks and IT incubation or training centres across Bangladesh. Startups and technology companies can access facility-based workspace, infrastructure and government services; training and accelerator support depends on the centre or project.

name: iDEA Project
cohortTiming: No fixed cohort; grant and co-working applications run through the application portal, subject to current notices.
costOrEquity: Startup grant: up to BDT 10 lakh, non-equity and non-repayable; co-working is free for up to six months.
applicationPath: Apply through the iDEA portal. The startup-grant application asks for identity documents, a business description, short video, pitch deck and any available prototype or proof of concept.
notes: An ICT Division and Bangladesh Computer Council programme providing non-dilutive pre-seed funding and technical support to innovative, scalable Bangladesh startups. Separate services include mentoring, networking, free co-working space and access to hardware prototyping facilities.

name: Accelerating Asia Accelerator
benefits: Potential follow-on funding up to US$150,000
cohortTiming: Cohort 14 applications are open; interviews begin in August 2026, the programme starts in October and Demo Day is planned for January 2027.
costOrEquity: US$35,000 programme fee, deducted from the initial investment, plus 3% equity; the investment uses a post-money SAFE.
applicationPath: Apply through Accelerating Asia Ventures' Get Funded page for Cohort 14.
notes: A 100-day VC accelerator for high-growth, pre-Series A technology startups across South and Southeast Asia. It is designed for companies with evidence of execution or traction and combines capital with intensive growth, fundraising and regional-expansion support.
